title: How games end
blurb: A game can end four different ways. Learn all four, then deliver your first checkmates.
deeperTitle: Back-rank mate and luft; the Scholar's Mate trap

core.title: Four ways to win
body: Most games end in **checkmate**. But that is only one of four ways to win.
You also win if your opponent **resigns**, if their **clock runs out**, or if they **walk away** and never come back.
Today you will learn all four. First, the big one.

core.title: Checkmate: no way out
body: A king that is attacked is **in check**. It must get out of check straight away.
There are only three ways: **step away**, **block** the attack, or **capture** the piece giving check. If none of them works, it is **checkmate** and the game is over.

board.caption: Black's queen attacks the white king. White has no way out.

core.prompt: Black's king is in check. What happens next?
options: Checkmate: no way out
Not mate: the king can step away
Not mate: the king can capture the checker
Not mate: another piece can block
core.explain: The rook gives check along the e-file, but the king has free squares beside it. It simply **steps aside**.

core.prompt: Black's king is in check again. Is this the end?
options: Checkmate: no way out
Not mate: the king can step away
Not mate: the king can capture the checker
Not mate: another piece can block
core.explain: Every square around the king is covered, but the queen is right next to it and **nothing protects her**. The king just takes her.

options: Checkmate: no way out
Not mate: the king can step away
Not mate: the king can capture the checker
Not mate: another piece can block
core.explain: The king is boxed in by its own pieces and cannot reach the rook. But the bishop can jump in front of the check on e6. That is a **block**.

options: Checkmate: no way out
Not mate: the king can step away
Not mate: the king can capture the checker
Not mate: another piece can block
core.explain: The queen is **protected by the white king**, so Black's king cannot capture her. Every other square next to it is covered. That is **checkmate**.

core.prompt: Your king is in check from the rook. Get out of it by blocking.
core.hint: Your king has no free squares. Which piece can step in front of the rook?
core.explain: **Be3** blocks the e-file. When your king is boxed in and cannot capture the checker, a block is your way out.

core.prompt: The queen gives check, and she is next to your king. Get out of check.
core.hint: Your king cannot take her, because the bishop protects her. Who else can capture on e2?
core.explain: **Nxe2** captures the queen. The bishop takes the knight back, but you traded a knight for a queen. Capturing the checker can win material, too.

core.prompt: Checkmate in one. Your king is helping.
core.hint: Put the queen on a square next to the black king that your own king also guards.
core.explain: **Qg7#**. The queen attacks the king, your king protects her, and no square is left to run to.

core.prompt: Checkmate in one. The queen needs a partner this time.
core.hint: Which black pawn is attacked twice, by the queen and by the bishop?
core.explain: **Qxh7#**. The bishop on d3 protects the queen, and the black pieces are blocking their own king's escape squares.

core.title: Three more ways to win
body: **Resignation.** A player gives up because they are clearly losing. You win. It saves everyone time.
**Time.** Every game has a clock. If yours hits zero you lose, even if you are ahead on the board.
**Abandonment.** If your opponent leaves and never comes back, you win.

core.prompt: You are up a queen, but your clock runs out. What is the result?
options: You win, because you are ahead
You lose on time
It is a draw
core.explain: The clock is part of the game. Being ahead on the board does not save you. (There is one rare exception, which you will meet on Day 7.)

core.prompt: Your opponent closes the app and never comes back. What happens?
options: It is a draw
You win once the site declares them gone
You have to resign
core.explain: Walking away is called **abandonment**. Online, the site gives them a little time to return, then awards you the win.

core.prompt: Which of these ends the game with a win for you?
options: You capture their queen
Their king is in check
They resign
core.explain: Winning the queen or giving check does not end the game. Only checkmate, resignation, time or abandonment do.

core.prompt: Black's king is in check. Tap the piece giving check.
core.explain: The queen on h5 sees along the diagonal all the way to the king on e8.

core.title: Checkmate in one
core.intro: Three quick ones. Find the move that ends the game.

puzzles.hint: Your king already covers the squares in front of the black king.
puzzles.explain: The king on b6 guards a7 and b7, so the rook only has to check along the back rank.

puzzles.hint: White's king is exposed on the diagonal.
puzzles.explain: White's pawn moves opened a diagonal straight to the king. This is the quickest checkmate in chess.

puzzles.hint: Look at where the bishop is aiming.
puzzles.explain: The bishop on b2 protects g7 along the long diagonal, so the queen cannot be taken.

deeper.title: The back-rank mate
body: This is the most common checkmate at every level. The king stays on its back rank, behind a wall of its own pawns. Then a rook or queen arrives on that rank and the king has nowhere to go.

board.caption: The pawns that were meant to protect the king now trap it.

deeper.prompt: Checkmate in one. Use the open file.
deeper.hint: Which rank is the black king stuck on?
deeper.explain: **Rd8#**. The rook checks along the back rank and the king's own pawns block every escape.

deeper.prompt: Checkmate in one. Their rook is in the way, but that can change.
deeper.hint: Can you take the rook and give check at the same time?
deeper.explain: **Rxc8#**. Capturing with check ends the game, because Black has nothing left to recapture with.

deeper.prompt: White threatens Rd8 checkmate. Find a move that stops it.
deeper.hint: Give the king somewhere to run.
deeper.explain: Moving a pawn to give your king an escape square is called making **luft** (German for "air"). Any pawn move on the f, g or h file works. Only stepping to h8 walks into mate.

puzzles.explain: The black pawns trap their own king.

puzzles.hint: Black can use the same trick against White.
puzzles.explain: White forgot to make luft, so the back rank falls.

puzzles.hint: The queen also travels along files.
puzzles.explain: A queen does the job of a rook here.

deeper.title: Scholar's Mate: the trap everyone falls for once
body: At the start of the game, the pawn on **f7** is protected only by the king. That makes it the weakest point in Black's camp.
A quick attack with the queen and the bishop can aim at f7 and mate in four moves. Beginners both **play it** and **fall for it**, so learn to spot it.

board.caption: After 1.e4 e5. Both sides have opened the diagonals.

deeper.prompt: The white bishop is aiming at one black pawn. Tap it.
deeper.explain: Only the black king guards f7. If the queen joins the bishop, f7 falls.

deeper.prompt: Black just blundered with Nf6. Finish the game.
deeper.hint: The queen and the bishop both attack f7.
deeper.explain: **Qxf7#**. The bishop protects the queen, and the king's escape squares are blocked by its own pieces.

deeper.prompt: You are Black. White threatens Qxf7 checkmate. Stop it.
deeper.hint: Defend f7, or chase the queen away.
deeper.explain: The simplest answers are **Qe7** or **Nh6**, which defend f7, or **g6**, which kicks the queen. Nf6 looks active, but it leaves f7 hanging.

deeper.prompt: What is the best habit against Scholar's Mate?
options: Always play the same first move
Check f7 (or f2) every time a queen and a bishop line up
Never move your king's pawn
deeper.explain: A quick look at f7 before every move in the first few turns will save you from this trap for life.
